subject: spanish
topicDisplay: Context 3 School Life Studies And The World Of Work
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does “el colegio mixto” mean?
questions.explain: “Mixto” = mixed, so “el colegio mixto” = “a co-educational school” (boys and girls).

questions.q: Which sentence means “I find maths difficult”?
questions.explain: “Me resultan difíciles” = “I find them difficult”; the verb agrees with the plural “las matemáticas”.

questions.q: How would you write 'trabajador' to describe a hard-working woman?
questions.explain: Adjectives ending in -dor add -a for the feminine singular, so a hard-working woman is 'trabajadora'.

questions.q: Which means “If I studied more, I would pass”?
questions.explain: Unreal condition: imperfect subjunctive “estudiara” + conditional “aprobaría”.

questions.q: Which means “The pay is low but I enjoy the work”?
options: El sueldo es bajo pero odio el trabajo
El sueldo es bajo pero disfruto del trabajo
El sueldo es alto pero disfruto del trabajo
El suelo es bajo pero disfruto del trabajo
questions.explain: “El sueldo es bajo” = the pay is low and “disfruto del trabajo” = I enjoy the work.

questions.q: What does “una entrevista de trabajo” mean?
questions.explain: “Una entrevista” = an interview, so “una entrevista de trabajo” = “a job interview”.

questions.q: How do you say “We wear a uniform”?
questions.explain: “Llevar” = “to wear” and “llevamos” = “we wear”, so “Llevamos uniforme”.

questions.q: What does 'el desempleo' mean?
questions.explain: 'El desempleo' (also 'el paro') means 'unemployment'; 'el empleo' is 'employment/a job'.

questions.q: Which means “The rules are very strict”?
questions.explain: “Las normas” = the rules and “estrictas” = strict.

questions.q: Which means “I would earn more money if I spoke languages”?
options: Ganaría más dinero si hablo idiomas
Gano más dinero si hablo idiomas
Ganaría más dinero si hablara idiomas
Ganaré más dinero si hablara idiomas
questions.explain: An unreal condition uses conditional + imperfect subjunctive: “ganaría... si hablara”.

questions.q: What does “la pizarra” mean?
questions.explain: “La pizarra” means “the board/whiteboard” in the classroom.

questions.q: What does “el/la jefe” mean?
questions.explain: “El jefe” means “the boss”; a chef/cook is “el cocinero” (false friend).

questions.q: What does “el director” mean in a school context?
questions.explain: At school “el director” means “the headteacher/principal”.

questions.q: What does 'el éxito' mean?
questions.explain: 'El éxito' is a false friend: it means 'success', not 'exit' (which is 'la salida').

questions.q: What does “el sueldo” mean?
questions.explain: “El sueldo” means “the salary/wage”; “el suelo” (floor) is a near-miss distractor.

questions.q: What does “ganarse la vida” mean?
questions.explain: “Ganarse la vida” is an idiom meaning “to earn a living”.

questions.q: What does “el aprendizaje” most commonly mean?
questions.explain: “El aprendizaje” means “learning”, and in a work context “an apprenticeship”.

questions.q: What does “la asignatura” mean?
questions.explain: “La asignatura” means “a school subject”; it is a false friend with “signature” (la firma).

questions.q: What does “el desempleo” mean?
questions.explain: “El desempleo” means “unemployment” (also “el paro”).

questions.q: What does 'el ocio' mean?
questions.explain: 'El ocio' means 'leisure / free time'; it is a false friend with English 'office' (which is 'la oficina').

questions.q: What does “la nota” mean in “mi nota de inglés”?
questions.explain: In school Spanish “la nota” means “the mark/grade”.

questions.q: What does 'la asignatura' mean?
questions.explain: 'La asignatura' is a false friend: it means 'school subject', not 'signature' (which is 'la firma').
